---
title: "Childcare costs"
description: "What families pay for childcare after state supports, compared with other EU countries."
---

In 2023/2024, childcare for a child under 3 in Ireland cost an average of €491 a month after state supports, according to Eurydice, the European Commission's network on education systems. For children aged 3 and over the average was €331 a month, on top of the free preschool hours of the Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) scheme.

Adjusted for differences in prices between countries, the fee for under-3s in Ireland was the highest of the 16 EU countries that give a single average figure. Eurydice records no fees for under-3s in Bulgaria, Latvia, Portugal and Romania.

{{< chart childcare-fees-eu >}}

## Fees in Ireland over time

Pobal, which administers the State's childcare funding schemes, surveys childcare services every year. In 2020/21 the average weekly fee for one child in full day care was €187, compared with €166 in 2011. These are full fees, including any part paid by State subsidies such as ECCE.

Pobal published these figures in a yearly report until 2020/21. From 2021/22 the report was replaced by online dashboards, which have no option to download the figures, so the charts on this page stop at 2020/21. Since September 2022, services in the Core Funding scheme have had their fees capped at the level they charged in September 2021.

{{< chart childcare-fees-trend >}}

## Fees by county

Fees were highest in the four Dublin council areas and Wicklow. In 2020/21 the average weekly fee for full day care was €244 in Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown and €152 in Carlow.

{{< chart childcare-fees-county >}}

The fees take account of the National Childcare Scheme, which pays a subsidy towards the cost of registered childcare, and of the ECCE scheme. Families' own costs depend on the child's age, the hours used, the provider and, for income-based subsidies, household income.
